label: prf:feynman-markov-identification
title: Proof that the eigenbasis amplitude equals the Markov trace
html:
Proof. Proof that the eigenbasis amplitude equals the Markov trace

Proof. The Jones--Markov trace is the unique trace on \bigcup_n H_n(R, q) satisfying the Markov property \mathrm{tr}_M(x \sigma_n^{\pm 1}) = z^{\pm 1}\mathrm{tr}_M(x) (Jones--Markov trace). By the Wedderburn-Artin decomposition of the semisimple algebra H_n(R, q), every trace decomposes as a weighted sum of irreducible characters:

  \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(\rho(\beta)\bigr)
  =
  \sum_{\substack{\lambda \vdash n \\ \ell(\lambda) \leq 2}}
  w_\lambda \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{S_\lambda}\bigl(\rho_n(\beta)\bigr),

where the Markov weights w_\lambda are uniquely determined by the Markov property and the normalisation \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1. The Markov weights encode the quantum dimensions: w_\lambda = \dim_q(V_\lambda) \cdot \dim(S_\lambda) / \dim_q(V^{\otimes n}).

The transition amplitude on the eigenbasis, defined as the Markov-weighted sum of partial traces, therefore equals the Markov trace by construction:

  \langle\psi_f|\psi_i\rangle_{\mathrm{eigenbasis}}
  :=
  \sum_\lambda w_\lambda \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{S_\lambda}\bigl(\rho_n(\beta)\bigr)
  =
  \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(\rho(\beta)\bigr).

The content of this identification is not tautological: it says that the unique measure on the finite eigenbasis that satisfies the Markov property (and hence gives topological link invariants) is the one that replaces the Feynman path measure. \square
